title: Shifting Letters II
summary: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters and a 2D array shifts, for each shift operation, move the characters in the specified range forward or backward in the alphabet.
statement: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters and a 2D array shifts, for each shift operation, move the characters in the specified range forward or backward in the alphabet. For forward shifts, replace each character with the next one; for backward shifts, replace with the previous one. Wrap around the alphabet if necessary. Apply all shifts to the string and return the modified string.
constraints: Direction 1 shifts letters forward; direction 0 shifts backward.
Alphabet shifts wrap between a and z; return the string after all operations.
hints: Record +delta at each range start and -delta just after its inclusive end.
Take a prefix sum to obtain the net shift at each character.
Add that net value modulo 26 to produce the final letter.
Difference updates include every operation in constant time, and prefix accumulation applies exactly the operations covering each position.
editorial: Difference updates include every operation in constant time, and prefix accumulation applies exactly the operations covering each position.

tests.explanation: The net shifts are zero, one, and two positions, producing ace.
A forward shift wraps z to a.
